turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Doctor. Well, I'm here because my eating habits have gotten pretty restricted lately. I'm a firefighter, and originally, I just wanted to start eating cleaner to get in better shape for the lieutenant track. But it's kind of turned into me cutting my meals down to almost nothing. 

Lately, I'm basically just having black coffee, a protein shake, and a really small dinner. And I'm doing that even on shift days, when we're running calls and I know for a fact I've burned way more energy than what I'm taking in. It just feels like it went a bit too far, so I figured I should come in.

symptom_reasoning.S043: The patient explicitly describes restricting food intake down to black coffee, a protein shake, and a small dinner despite high energy expenditure on shift days.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been avoiding eating more because you're worried about gaining weight or becoming fat?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I am. Honestly, if I step on the scale and it's up even just a pound—like, maybe after a big meal at the station or just from drinking extra water—I get this... this tight panic. It just feels like I’ve completely blown it. I worry that if I gain weight, people are going to see me as soft, or like I'm just out of control of myself. So, yeah, that fear is definitely a big part of why I avoid eating more.

symptom_reasoning.S045: The patient explicitly confirms experiencing panic and intense fear over gaining even a single pound, noting that this fear directly causes them to avoid eating more.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been doing anything else like exercising a lot, making yourself vomit, or using laxatives or diet pills to try to control your weight?
turns.patient_response: No, I haven't done any of that. I don't make myself throw up, and I don't take laxatives or diet pills or anything like that. I do work out, but it's just my normal routine for the job—I wouldn't say I'm exercising excessively on top of what I already do at the station. It's really just the restricting what I eat.

symptom_reasoning.S043: The patient confirms restricting food intake by stating that their weight control method is 'really just the restricting what I eat.'
symptom_reasoning.S047: The patient explicitly denies excessive exercise, clarifying their workout is only their normal routine for work.
symptom_reasoning.S048: The patient explicitly denies purging behaviors, stating they do not make themselves throw up or take laxatives or diet pills.

turns.doctor_question: Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently, or is your weight currently lower than what would be considered healthy for someone your height and build?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I have lost quite a bit. I started noticing it when my gear and my station clothes started hanging a lot looser on me. We just had our annual fitness review, and they actually flagged my weight as being too low for my height and build. But honestly, even with them telling me that, part of me still feels like I need to keep trimming down just a little bit more.

symptom_reasoning.S044: The patient confirms significant weight loss resulting in clothes hanging loose, an official fitness review flagging their weight as too low for their build, and a desire to continue trimming down.

turns.doctor_question: Do you see yourself as overweight or notice specific parts of your body that you feel are too big, even if others might not see it that way?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, I do. I mean, I might not see my whole body as overweight, but... well, when I look in the mirror before work, I really zero in on specific parts. Mostly my waist and my face. 

I check to see if they look sharp enough, like there's no extra softness there. And if they don't look right to me, if I feel like they look too big... it really messes with my head. It just kind of ruins how confident I feel. I just don't feel as command-ready for the shift if I think I look soft in those areas.

symptom_reasoning.S046: The patient confirms zeroing in on specific body parts (waist and face) as looking too big/soft, which directly impairs their confidence and self-evaluation.

turns.doctor_question: How much does your perception of your body shape or weight influence your sense of self-worth or how you judge yourself?
turns.patient_response: It honestly influences it a lot. Like I mentioned, if I look in the mirror before a shift and my waist or face don't look sharp enough... it just completely throws me off. If I feel like I look soft or too big in those areas, I just don't feel confident. I feel like I'm not ready to lead or take command at work. My whole sense of how good I am at my job, or just how I feel about myself that day, really rides on how I think I look in the mirror.

turns.doctor_question: Is your main concern about restricting your food intake related to gaining weight, or is it more about achieving a specific look or level of muscle definition, even if that doesn’t necessarily involve gaining or losing fat?

turns.doctor_question: Have you found yourself thinking about food, weight, or body shape so much that it interferes with your ability to focus on other things, like work or relationships?
